thread:
vikram: quick q — for the new request logging sampler, do we want per-route UI controls or global knobs only?
anya: i'd prefer per-route. different endpoints have wildly different PII risk and traffic profiles.
sam: per-route + inheritance. default global policy, routes can opt-in overrides. avoids UI explosion.
ellie: +1 for inheritance. also need a way to see effective policy in console (what actually applies).
jordan: logging concern: if we let route-level increase sampling, cost could spike. need quota guardrails.
vikram: yep — proposal: route-level target sampling rate + route max tokens budget (monthly). console shows projected cost delta.
anya: can we show "estimated tokens" per route in the UI using the last 7 days traffic distribution? would help decisions.
sam: technically doable. use offline job to compute median response length per route and use qps to estimate. update daily.
ellie: question on debugging: how do we ensure deterministic capture for trace reconstruction? random sampling loses linkability.
jordan: suggestion: support deterministic hash sampling for a subset of fields (e.g., customer_id) so you can capture all requests for a customer consistently.
vikram: love that. but hash retention = PII risk. we should store only a salted hash and allow rotation.
anya: need opt-out for regulated customers. their routes should be forced to redact before any hashing.
sam: redaction mechanics: prefer field-level regex redaction + structured mask markers rather than free text removal. keeps context.
ellie: agree. sample config idea: 

```
logging:
  default_sampler: 0.01
  routes:
    /ingest/*:
      sampler: 0.1
      max_monthly_token_budget: 500000
      redact:
        - path: $.payment.card_number
          method: regex
          pattern: "\\d{12,19}"
        - path: $.user.email
          method: mask
```

vikram: that config looks good. need to validate that redact rules run before sampling so we never write raw PII to logs.
jordan: absolutely. pipeline order must be redact -> hash -> sample -> store. add audit log for every redaction rule hit.
anya: audit logs are sensitive too. they should be encrypted and accessible only to EUD/Security with breakglass.
ops-bot: deploy queued: config-service v1.42 -> staging at 2026-03-19T21:04:15Z :gear:
vikram: ops-bot, can we run a canary: enable per-route override in staging only for team accounts and run for 24h?
ops-bot: canary started for team:platform. routes: /ingest/*, /eval/*, override_sampler=0.2, duration=24h.
sam: UX note — in console rollout screen, show the effective sampling multiplier and estimated ingestion per hour, plus a warning if estimated monthly cost > 10% baseline.
ellie: also add a "show raw example request after redaction" toggle so reviewers can verify redaction effectiveness without seeing PII. show masked values only.
jordan: on retention: default dropped logs kept 7 days, sampled stored 90 days. enterprise can request longer via private deployment.
vikram: follow-up: deterministic sampling uses salted hash of (route + customer_id) mod 100 < 10 for 10% — need to document rotation plan for salt and effects on trace continuity.
anya: doc action: i'll draft a short doc covering pipeline order, UI controls, quota guardrails, deterministic sampling, and audit controls. will ping for review.
sam: dev action: i'll add console mockups of the route policy panel and cost projection widget.
ellie: eng action: i'll add unit tests for redact-first pipeline and add an e2e that asserts no raw PII is ever persisted.
vikram: thanks. final ask: can we add a console hover tooltip that explains "Why am I not seeing X request in logs?" — show sampling decision and redaction hits. small UX win.
jordan: documented. sounding good. :thumbsup:
